title: Career Roadmap: Editor
summary: Career Domain: Media, Communication, Arts & Design Qualification Pathway: B.Voc – Media / Film Production / Sound Target Career: Editor Career ID: 2476

blocks.text: An Editor selects, organises, refines, and assembles recorded footage, audio, images, or other media into a coherent final product. Depending on the specialisation, an editor may work on films, television programmes, advertisements, documentaries, YouTube videos, podcasts, music videos, or digital media content.
For a student pursuing a B.Voc in Media, Film Production, or Sound, the most relevant pathways include video editing, film editing, audio editing, and post-production.
Video and Film Editor

items.text: Select and arrange shots into a compelling sequence.
Synchronise footage with dialogue, music, and sound effects.
Collaborate with directors, cinematographers, and producers.

blocks.text: Audio Editor

items.text: Clean dialogue and remove unwanted noise.
Edit interviews, podcasts, voice-overs, and sound effects.
Prepare audio files for final mixing and delivery.

rows.text: Sound Editor / Documentary Editor / Commercial Editor

blocks.text: Progression depends on portfolio quality, practical experience, storytelling ability, and the complexity of projects handled—not solely on the qualification.
The following plan assumes a three-year B.Voc programme. Adjust it to the institution's actual duration and curriculum.
Year 1 — Editing Fundamentals

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Learn the language of visual storytelling and the fundamentals of editing.

rows.text: Shot types, camera angles, framing, continuity
Resolution, frame rate, aspect ratio, codecs
Dialogue levels, music, ambience, sound effects
Exposure, white balance, contrast, colour correction
Folders, naming conventions, backups, media organisation
Understanding briefs, receiving feedback, meeting deadlines

blocks.text: Software to explore

items.text: CapCut Desktop, where appropriate for short-form content

blocks.text: Practical projects

items.text: Create a one-minute montage using original footage.
Edit an interview with clean dialogue and suitable cutaways.
Produce a short video with music, titles, and end credits.
Create two versions of the same footage with different pacing.

blocks.label: Year 1 outcome
blocks.text: Ability to complete basic edits, organise media, export correctly, and explain fundamental editing decisions.
Year 2 — Professional Editing and Post-Production

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Develop the skills required for client projects and professional production workflows.

rows.text: J-cuts, L-cuts, match cuts, montage, narrative pacing
Shot matching, skin tones, scopes, creative looks
Dialogue cleanup, noise reduction, ambience, mixing basics
Animated titles, lower thirds, simple visual effects
Review notes, project handoffs, shared media workflows

blocks.text: Practical projects

items.text: Produce a polished podcast or interview episode.
Create three short-form social media edits from one source recording.
Edit a product advertisement with sound design and colour correction.
Prepare subtitles and alternate exports for different platforms.

blocks.label: Year 2 outcome
blocks.text: Ability to handle multi-track projects, maintain continuity, improve audio and colour, and deliver edits according to a production brief.
Year 3 — Specialisation and Industry Readiness

blocks.label: Objective
blocks.text: Build a professional portfolio and prepare for employment or freelance work.

rows.text: Character development, emotional pacing, documentary structure
Film, advertising, social media, music videos, or audio post-production
Keyboard shortcuts, templates, proxy workflows, automation
Brief interpretation, revisions, deadlines, scope management
File handoffs, feedback cycles, project documentation

blocks.label: Capstone project
blocks.text: Produce a complete post-production portfolio featuring three to five carefully selected projects.
For each project, include:

items.text: The original brief and intended audience
The creative decisions behind pacing, music, sound, and colour
A short reflection on feedback and improvements

blocks.label: Year 3 outcome
blocks.text: A job-ready portfolio, practical post-production experience, and the ability to present editing decisions professionally.

rows.text: Advanced in at least one tool
Prevents missing files and workflow delays
Detects continuity, timing, and export issues
Video editing, colour grading, audio post-production
Professional video editing and production workflows
Basic audio editing and noise processing

blocks.label: Recommended strategy
blocks.text: Start with one main video editor and learn it deeply before trying multiple applications. DaVinci Resolve is a useful starting option because it offers editing, colour, and audio tools within one application. Check current hardware requirements and licensing before choosing software.

rows.text: Student media team or campus production
Production house, digital agency, or creator team
Film post-production studio, media company, or freelance projects

blocks.text: Potential workplaces include film production houses, advertising agencies, television studios, digital media companies, YouTube production teams, podcast studios, and corporate video departments.
Internship deliverables to aim for

items.text: A project showing audio cleanup and sound design

blocks.text: Use footage you own, footage licensed for your intended use, or material explicitly provided for portfolio work. Obtain permission before publishing client work.
For editors, the portfolio often carries substantial weight in recruitment.
A strong portfolio should contain:

blocks.label: Showreel
blocks.text: A concise compilation of your strongest work.

blocks.label: Narrative project
blocks.text: Demonstrates continuity, pacing, and storytelling.

blocks.label: Commercial project
blocks.text: Demonstrates brand communication and concise messaging.

blocks.label: Interview or documentary
blocks.text: Demonstrates dialogue editing and story structure.

blocks.label: Specialist sample
blocks.text: Demonstrates your preferred direction, such as sound editing, colour grading, or motion graphics.

For every project, clearly distinguish your own contribution from work completed by collaborators. Do not use transitions or visual effects simply to make the showreel look complex; demonstrate purposeful editing choices.
Useful areas for additional training include:

items.text: Copyright, music licensing, and media rights

blocks.text: Prioritise practical assignments and assessed portfolio work over collecting certificates without demonstrable skills.
After completing the B.Voc, possible options include:

rows.text: MA / PG programme in Film or Media Production
Broader production knowledge and creative development
Specialisation in dialogue, ambience, and sound effects
Access to motion-design and compositing projects
Preparation for production coordination and supervision

blocks.text: Programme eligibility and admission requirements vary by institution.
Potential entry-level and specialist roles include:

items.text: Motion Graphics Editor, with additional skills

blocks.text: Editors may work as salaried employees, freelancers, contractors, or independent post-production business owners.

blocks.label: AI-assisted editing
blocks.text: Automated transcripts, rough cuts, scene detection, and captioning.

blocks.label: Short-form video
blocks.text: Editing for vertical formats and audience retention.

blocks.label: Cloud collaboration
blocks.text: Remote review, shared project files, and distributed production teams.

blocks.label: Virtual production
blocks.text: Editing and finishing workflows connected with real-time production technologies.

blocks.label: Accessibility
blocks.text: Captions, subtitles, readable titles, and accessible content versions.

blocks.label: Content localisation
blocks.text: Multiple language versions, dubbing, and subtitle workflows.
AI tools can speed up repetitive tasks, but editors still need to make creative decisions, verify automated outputs, respect licensing restrictions, and protect confidential footage.
Editor readiness
Explain continuity, pacing, shot selection, and visual storytelling.
Complete an edit using one primary editing application.
Clean dialogue and balance music with spoken audio.
Perform basic colour correction and match shots.
Export videos in the correct aspect ratio, resolution, and codec.
Organise project files and maintain backups.
Complete at least three portfolio projects with clearly defined personal contributions.
Complete an internship or practical production assignment.
Respond professionally to revision notes and deadlines.
Understand basic copyright, music licensing, and client confidentiality.
B.Voc – Media / Film Production / Sound
Technical fundamentals and production practice
Editing Intern / Junior Editor
Basic editing, file organisation, revisions
Video Editor / Assistant Film Editor
Independent editing assignments
Senior Editor / Specialist Editor
Complex projects and creative responsibility
Lead Editor / Post-Production Supervisor
Team leadership, quality control, production workflows
By graduation, the student should aim to have:

items.text: Strong practical ability in one professional editing application.
A portfolio of three to five well-finished projects.
Working knowledge of audio cleanup, colour correction, captions, and exports.
Experience handling briefs, revisions, and deadlines.
An internship or supervised production experience.
Basic knowledge of media rights, licensing, and file management.
A defined specialisation, such as film, advertising, digital content, or audio post-production.

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: For a B.Voc student targeting an Editor role, prioritise editing fundamentals, storytelling, software proficiency, and a demonstrable portfolio. These capabilities will generally provide a stronger employment foundation than software knowledge or certificates alone.
